pr_title: Fix ssl_do_config and SSL_load_client_CA_file_ex changing library context
pr_body:
Do not change the current default library context when NULL is passed as the library context to use. Also do not restore the previous library context when it was not changed before.

Fixes #14593

Why is that necessary? You can of course always do that if you have previously called `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` when the default default context was already set and saved away the return value - which is the intended way that `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` is supposed to be used.

issue_context.title: SSL_CTX_new is unexpectedly changing the current library context
issue_context.body:
`SSL_CTX_new()` and `SSL_CTX_new_ex()` does change the current library context to the initial default library context under some circumstances:

`SSL_CTX_new_ex()` calls `ssl_ctx_system_config()` which in turn calls `ssl_do_config()`. In `ssl_do_config()`, somewhere in the middle of the function, it uses `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` to set the current library context to the one from the SSL context, and remembers the previous library context in `prev_libctx`. Further down (at the `err` label) it restores the previous library context to what it was before (i.e. `prev_libctx`).

So far so good, but if the function fails early, i.e. before initially setting the library context via `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()`, it did not change the current library context, and thus did not remember the previous context,  but at the `err` label it unconditionally restores the previous library context to `prev_libctx`, which is then NULL.  

However, calling `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` with NULL changes the current library context to the initial default library context. So if a different library context was set up before and set as current one, it is now no longer the current one. It should not be assumed that calling `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default` with NULL would be a no-op.

In my case it is failing at `conf_ssl_name_find()` to find the `"system_default"`, for whatever reason. It then goes to the `err` label and thus changes the current library context to NULL. Since I loaded my own provider only into my own library context, it won't find my provider from now on.

This problem was introduced with commit 6725682d77510bf6d499957897d7be124d603f40 as far as I can tell.

There are some other similar places with similar invalid restoring of the default library context:
- `SSL_load_client_CA_file_ex()` (ssl/ssl_cert.c) unconditionally restores the library context at the done label.  If the function fails early, it also calls `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default`  with NULL (also since commit 6725682d77510bf6d499957897d7be124d603f40).
- `ASYNC_start_job()` (crypto/async/asyc.c) sets and restores the library context, but if `async_fibre_swapcontext()` fails, it did change the library context, but does not restore the previous one at the err label (since commit 6c689e58f70726cfa5533bc10f9669abce199fb8).

I'd just add `ctx->currjob->libctx = OPENSSL_CTX_set0_default(libctx);` before the `goto err;` to restore the previous libctx.
maybe with additional `if (libctx != NULL)` before both these calls as that NULL indicates failure of the original set call.
I'll submit PR for that one.

`libctx = OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default(ctx->currjob->libctx);`

Can `ctx->currjob->libctx` be NULL? If so, then you don't want to call OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default at all, because that would set the initial lib context, but that's possibly not what is desired?

> Can ctx->currjob->libctx be NULL?

No. That isn't possible (except in an error condition).

review_comments: No. `prev_libctx == NULL && libctx != NULL` can happen only if OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default() fails which means the prev_libctx is not meaningful anyway. And there are code paths which can get here where the OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default() was not called at all.

Logically I find this strange. In my mind the condition for checking whether to set a new default lib ctx should be the same for deciding whether to reset it on exit. It is odd to use different conditions IMO.

Either way, should we be testing for prev_libctx being NULL after the first `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` and erroring out in that case?

> Either way, should we be testing for prev_libctx being NULL after the first `OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default()` and erroring out in that case?

Yes, that would make sense. But this condition should be still kept.
